01-02.text: The Soviet Union launched Luna 1, which would fly past the Moon and enter orbit around the Sun.

01-03.text: Ohio's Frances Bolton and her son Oliver began serving together in the U.S. House of Representatives.

01-04.text: The Doors released their self-titled debut album.

01-05.text: Nellie Tayloe Ross took office in Wyoming, becoming America's first female governor.

01-06.text: Pan American introduced a round-the-world airline ticket.

01-07.text: Edison's studio filmed a sneeze, an early experiment in motion pictures.

01-08.text: Ella Grasso took office as governor of Connecticut.

01-09.text: NASA announced plans for the powerful C-5 rocket, later named Saturn V.

01-10.text: Project Diana successfully bounced radio signals off the Moon.

01-11.text: American League owners approved baseball's designated hitter rule.

01-12.text: Downtown Disney opened at California's Disneyland Resort.

01-13.text: Space shuttle Endeavour lifted off on mission STS-54.

01-14.text: Elvis Presley's Aloha from Hawaii concert was broadcast live by satellite.

01-15.text: Green Bay defeated Kansas City 35-10 in the first Super Bowl.

01-16.text: Soyuz 4 and Soyuz 5 docked in orbit, and two cosmonauts transferred between them during a spacewalk.

01-17.text: Prohibition began in the United States.

01-18.text: Willie O'Ree broke the NHL's color barrier when he debuted with the Boston Bruins.

01-19.text: I Love Lucy aired its hugely popular episode in which Lucy gives birth.

01-20.text: The National Negro Network launched with 40 radio stations.

01-21.text: Britain's rebuilt Emley Moor television transmitter began UHF broadcasts.

01-22.text: Teddy Wakelam gave live radio commentary on Arsenal's soccer match against Sheffield United.

01-23.text: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducted its first class, including Elvis Presley and Chuck Berry.

01-24.text: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security began operations.

01-25.text: The Guiding Light began on NBC radio, years before becoming a television soap opera.

01-26.text: John Logie Baird demonstrated his television system in London.

01-27.text: The Lockheed P-38 Lightning made its first flight.

01-28.text: Elvis Presley made his national television debut.

01-29.text: Baseball announced the first inductees into its Hall of Fame.

01-30.text: The Beatles played their rooftop concert at Apple Records in London.

01-31.text: NBC broadcast These Are My Children, an early daytime television soap opera.

02-01.text: I Want to Hold Your Hand became the Beatles' first U.S. number-one hit.

02-02.text: Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, held its first Groundhog Day observance.

02-03.text: Space shuttle Challenger launched on mission STS-41-B.

02-04.text: The Electoral College unanimously chose George Washington as the first U.S. president.

02-05.text: The Royal Greenwich Observatory began broadcasting its familiar time signals.

02-06.text: Jack Kilby filed a patent application for an integrated circuit.

02-07.text: The Beatles arrived at New York's JFK Airport for their first U.S. visit.

02-08.text: The Boy Scouts of America was incorporated.

02-09.text: The Beatles made their first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show.

02-10.text: IBM's Deep Blue computer defeated Garry Kasparov in a chess game.

02-11.text: The Beatles held their marathon recording session for Please Please Me.

02-12.text: Construction began on the Gateway Arch in St. Louis.

02-13.text: Frank Selvy scored 100 points in a college basketball game.

02-14.text: The League of Women Voters was founded in Chicago.

02-15.text: New U.S. federal copyright protections for sound recordings took effect.

02-16.text: Wallace Carothers received a U.S. patent for nylon.

02-17.text: Vanguard 2 launched to study cloud cover from space.

02-18.text: The Belgian Olympic Committee was established in Brussels.

02-19.text: NASA's Mars Odyssey began mapping the Martian surface.

02-20.text: Emmett Ashford joined the Southwestern International League as an umpire, breaking a baseball barrier.

02-21.text: John Greenough received a U.S. patent for a sewing machine.

02-22.text: The U.S. hockey team beat the Soviet Union 4-3 in the Miracle on Ice.

02-23.text: Japan launched its WINDS communications satellite.

02-24.text: Space shuttle Discovery launched on its final mission, STS-133.

02-25.text: Samuel Colt received a U.S. patent for his revolver.

02-26.text: NASA launched AS-201, the first flight of a Saturn IB rocket.

02-27.text: Martin Kamen and Sam Ruben discovered carbon-14.

02-28.text: The final episode of M*A*S*H aired to an enormous television audience.

02-29.text: Hattie McDaniel became the first Black Academy Award winner, for Gone with the Wind.

03-01.text: Yellowstone was established as a national park.

03-02.text: King Kong premiered in New York City.

03-03.text: Apollo 9 launched to test the lunar module in Earth orbit.

03-04.text: A London newspaper published John Lennon's controversial interview about the Beatles' popularity.

03-05.text: George Westinghouse patented an air-brake system.

03-06.text: Svetlana Alliluyeva, Joseph Stalin's daughter, sought asylum at the U.S. embassy in India.

03-07.text: Alexander Graham Bell received his telephone patent.

03-08.text: Discovery launched with the International Space Station's Expedition 2 crew aboard.

03-09.text: Barbie made her debut at New York's American International Toy Fair.

03-10.text: Almon Strowger patented an automatic telephone switching system.

03-11.text: Endeavour launched with the first part of Japan's Kibo space-station laboratory.

03-12.text: The organization that became the Girl Scouts of the USA was founded.

03-13.text: William Herschel discovered the planet Uranus.

03-14.text: Eli Whitney received a patent for the cotton gin.

03-16.text: Wanderers beat Royal Engineers 1-0 in the first FA Cup final.

03-17.text: Vanguard 1 launched, becoming the first satellite powered by solar cells.

03-18.text: Alexei Leonov became the first person to make a spacewalk.

03-19.text: C-SPAN began televising proceedings of the U.S. House of Representatives.

03-20.text: USS Langley was commissioned as the U.S. Navy's first aircraft carrier.

03-21.text: Alan Freed's Moondog Coronation Ball brought an early rock-and-roll concert to Cleveland.

03-22.text: The Beatles released their debut album, Please Please Me.

03-23.text: Gus Grissom and John Young launched aboard Gemini 3.

03-24.text: Robert Koch announced his discovery of the bacterium that causes tuberculosis.

03-25.text: Coxey's Army began its protest march from Massillon, Ohio, toward Washington, D.C.

03-26.text: The United States launched the Explorer 3 satellite.

03-27.text: Helen Taft and Viscountess Chinda planted Japanese cherry trees in Washington, D.C.

03-28.text: The Vienna Philharmonic gave its first concert.

03-29.text: China's Terracotta Army was discovered in Shaanxi province.

03-30.text: The United States signed a treaty to buy Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million.

03-31.text: The U.S. Census Bureau received the first UNIVAC I computer.

04-01.text: TIROS-1 began sending television images of Earth's weather from orbit.

04-02.text: Congress passed the Coinage Act, establishing the U.S. Mint.

04-03.text: Motorola's Martin Cooper made a pioneering call on a handheld mobile phone.

04-04.text: The Beatles held all five top positions on the Billboard Hot 100.

04-05.text: Atlantis launched with the Compton Gamma Ray Observatory aboard.

04-06.text: The American League began using the designated hitter in regular-season baseball.

04-07.text: Marietta, Ohio, was founded in the Northwest Territory.

04-08.text: Hank Aaron hit his 715th home run, passing Babe Ruth's career total.

04-09.text: Marian Anderson performed her landmark concert at the Lincoln Memorial.

04-10.text: Paul McCartney's announcement signaled his break with the Beatles.

04-11.text: Apollo 13 lifted off on its mission toward the Moon.

04-12.text: Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space, orbiting Earth aboard Vostok 1.

04-13.text: Sidney Poitier won Best Actor at the Oscars for Lilies of the Field.

04-14.text: Columbia landed after the first space shuttle test flight.

04-15.text: Jackie Robinson made his Brooklyn Dodgers debut, breaking modern major-league baseball's color barrier.

04-16.text: Boston Arena opened its doors for the first time.

04-17.text: Apollo 13's crew returned safely to Earth after their damaged spacecraft's dramatic journey.

04-18.text: Jackie Robinson made his regular-season debut with the Montreal Royals.

04-19.text: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched into orbit.

04-20.text: Apollo 16 astronauts John Young and Charles Duke landed on the Moon.

04-22.text: People celebrated the first Earth Day.

04-23.text: Jawed Karim uploaded Me at the zoo, the first video on YouTube.

04-24.text: Space shuttle Discovery launched with the Hubble Space Telescope aboard.

04-25.text: New York introduced the first statewide U.S. requirement for automobile license plates.

04-26.text: Tanganyika and Zanzibar united, forming the country now called Tanzania.

04-27.text: Montreal held the opening ceremony for Expo 67.

04-28.text: Pink Floyd's The Dark Side of the Moon reached number one on the U.S. album chart.

04-29.text: Los Angeles viewers saw an experimental 3D television broadcast of Space Patrol.

04-30.text: NBC televised President Roosevelt's address at the opening of the New York World's Fair.

05-01.text: Coxey's Army of protesters arrived in Washington, D.C.

05-02.text: The Negro National League played its first baseball game, in Indianapolis.

05-03.text: Raja Harishchandra, a landmark in Indian feature-film history, was released.

05-04.text: The National Association opened its professional baseball season in Fort Wayne, Indiana.

05-05.text: Cy Young pitched a perfect game against the Philadelphia Athletics.

05-06.text: Babe Ruth hit his first major-league home run, while playing for Boston.

05-07.text: Space shuttle Endeavour launched on its first mission.

05-08.text: The Beatles released Let It Be.

05-09.text: Australia's first national parliament opened in Melbourne.

05-10.text: The golden spike ceremony at Promontory Summit marked completion of the U.S. transcontinental railroad.

05-11.text: Atlantis launched on the final mission to service the Hubble Space Telescope.

05-12.text: Konrad Zuse demonstrated his programmable Z3 computer in Berlin.

05-13.text: Robert Smalls escaped slavery by piloting the steamer Planter through Confederate lines to the U.S. Navy.

05-14.text: Skylab, America's first space station, launched into orbit.

05-15.text: Britain's experimental Gloster E.28/39 jet aircraft made its first flight.

05-16.text: Hollywood held the first Academy Awards ceremony.

05-17.text: Columbia and Princeton played a college baseball game televised in New York.

05-18.text: Apollo 10 launched on its lunar-landing rehearsal mission.

05-19.text: Marilyn Monroe sang Happy Birthday at a New York celebration for President John F. Kennedy.

05-20.text: Charles Lindbergh left New York aboard Spirit of St. Louis for his solo flight to Paris.

05-21.text: Charles Lindbergh landed in Paris, completing his solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic.

05-22.text: The Wright brothers received a U.S. patent for their flying machine.

05-23.text: Stanley Kubrick's The Shining opened in New York and Los Angeles.

05-24.text: The Reds beat the Phillies 2-1 at Crosley Field in Major League Baseball's first night game.

05-25.text: Star Wars opened in U.S. movie theaters.

05-26.text: The Beatles released Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band in Britain.

05-27.text: San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge opened to pedestrians.

05-28.text: The Dionne quintuplets were born near Callander, Ontario.

05-29.text: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit of Mount Everest.

05-30.text: Crew Dragon Demo-2 launched astronauts toward the International Space Station.

05-31.text: The Great Clock at London's Houses of Parliament began keeping time.

06-02.text: Surveyor 1 made America's first successful soft landing on the Moon.

06-03.text: Ed White made the first American spacewalk during the Gemini 4 mission.

06-04.text: Congress approved the 19th Amendment and sent the women's suffrage measure to the states.

06-05.text: Scientists created the first Bose-Einstein condensate.

06-06.text: Allied troops landed in Normandy on D-Day.

06-07.text: Spain and Portugal signed the Treaty of Tordesillas.

06-08.text: USS Barbero launched an experimental shipment of mail by missile.

06-09.text: Secretariat won the Belmont Stakes and completed horse racing's Triple Crown.

06-10.text: Alcoholics Anonymous traces its founding to this day in Akron, Ohio.

06-11.text: Edwin Armstrong demonstrated FM broadcasting to engineers in Washington, D.C.

06-12.text: Raiders of the Lost Ark arrived in movie theaters.

06-13.text: President Lyndon Johnson nominated Thurgood Marshall to the U.S. Supreme Court.

06-14.text: Disneyland's monorail opened to the public.

06-15.text: England's King John sealed Magna Carta.

06-16.text: The company that became IBM was founded as Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company.

06-17.text: Five burglars were arrested at the Democratic National Committee offices in the Watergate complex.

06-18.text: Sally Ride became the first American woman in space.

06-19.text: The Eagles and Steelers merged for one wartime NFL season.

06-21.text: The original London production of Evita opened.

06-22.text: Astronomer James Christy discovered Pluto's moon Charon.

06-23.text: The International Olympic Committee was founded in Paris.

06-24.text: The American Professional Football Association adopted the name National Football League.

06-25.text: Jay-Z released his debut album, Reasonable Doubt.

06-26.text: Elvis Presley gave his final concert, in Indianapolis.

06-27.text: The Baltimore and Ohio Railroad's Royal Blue began service between Washington and New York.

06-28.text: The Treaty of Versailles was signed.

06-29.text: Space shuttle Atlantis docked with Russia's Mir space station.

06-30.text: The National Organization for Women was founded.

07-01.text: Sony introduced the Walkman portable music player.

07-02.text: Live 8 benefit concerts were held around the world.

07-03.text: Karl Benz publicly unveiled his Patent-Motorwagen automobile.

07-04.text: The Second Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence.

07-05.text: Elvis Presley recorded That's All Right at Sun Records in Memphis.

07-06.text: Chicago hosted Major League Baseball's first All-Star Game.

07-07.text: Live Earth concerts brought musicians together at venues around the world.

07-08.text: Atlantis lifted off on the final space shuttle mission.

07-09.text: The first Wimbledon tennis championships began.

07-10.text: Telstar 1, an early communications satellite, launched into orbit.

07-11.text: Television images crossed the Atlantic by satellite.

07-12.text: Atlantis launched with the Quest airlock for the International Space Station.

07-13.text: Live Aid concerts united London and Philadelphia in a major music fundraiser.

07-14.text: A crowd stormed the Bastille in Paris during the French Revolution.

07-15.text: Boeing's 367-80 prototype, a forerunner of the 707, made its first flight.

07-16.text: Apollo 11 lifted off from Florida, bound for the Moon.

07-17.text: U.S. and Soviet spacecraft docked in orbit during the Apollo-Soyuz mission.

07-18.text: Nadia Comaneci earned the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics.

07-19.text: The women's rights convention opened in Seneca Falls, New York.

07-20.text: Apollo 11's Eagle landed on the Moon with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin aboard.

07-21.text: Gus Grissom flew into space aboard Liberty Bell 7.

07-22.text: Wiley Post completed the first solo airplane flight around the world.

07-23.text: Jackie Robinson was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame.

07-24.text: Apollo 11's crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean.

07-25.text: Bob Dylan performed an electric set at the Newport Folk Festival.

07-26.text: Disney's animated Alice in Wonderland premiered in London.

07-27.text: A Wild Hare introduced the familiar Bugs Bunny to movie audiences.

07-28.text: The 14th Amendment was formally certified as part of the U.S. Constitution.

07-29.text: President Eisenhower signed the law creating NASA.

07-30.text: President Lyndon Johnson signed Medicare and Medicaid into law.

07-31.text: Samuel Hopkins received the first U.S. patent, for a potash-making process.

08-01.text: MTV launched with the Buggles' Video Killed the Radio Star.

08-02.text: Delegates began signing the parchment copy of the Declaration of Independence.

08-03.text: Tandy announced the TRS-80 personal computer.

08-04.text: President Jimmy Carter signed the law creating the U.S. Department of Energy.

08-05.text: Cleveland installed a pioneering electric traffic signal.

08-06.text: Tim Berners-Lee publicly announced the World Wide Web project online.

08-08.text: Iain Macmillan photographed the Beatles on the crossing used for the Abbey Road album cover.

08-09.text: Jesse Owens won his fourth gold medal at the Berlin Olympics.

08-10.text: Candid Camera made its television debut.

08-11.text: Babe Ruth hit his 500th career home run at Cleveland's League Park.

08-13.text: East Germany closed the Berlin border as construction of the Berlin Wall began.

08-14.text: The American Football League held its first official meeting.

08-15.text: The Woodstock music festival opened in Bethel, New York.

08-16.text: The first issue of Sports Illustrated was published.

08-17.text: Michael Phelps won his eighth gold medal at the Beijing Olympics.

08-18.text: Tennessee's ratification secured the 19th Amendment, guaranteeing women's voting rights.

08-19.text: Dayton, Ohio, hosted the first All-American Soap Box Derby.

08-20.text: Football organizers met in Canton to form the American Professional Football Conference.

08-21.text: William Seward Burroughs received a patent for his adding machine.

08-22.text: Nolan Ryan became the first major-league pitcher to reach 5,000 career strikeouts.

08-23.text: The Lockheed C-130 made its first flight.

08-24.text: Amelia Earhart became the first woman to fly nonstop across the United States.

08-25.text: NASA launched the Spitzer Space Telescope.

08-26.text: John Fitch received a U.S. patent for a steamboat.

08-28.text: Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his I Have a Dream speech at the March on Washington.

08-29.text: The Beatles played their final ticketed concert at San Francisco's Candlestick Park.

08-30.text: Guion Bluford became the first Black American in space aboard Challenger.

09-01.text: A joint French-American expedition discovered the wreck of Titanic.

09-02.text: CBS expanded its evening television news to half an hour.

09-03.text: The United States and Britain signed the Treaty of Paris ending the Revolutionary War.

09-04.text: Swimmer Mark Spitz won his seventh gold medal at the Munich Olympics.

09-05.text: Voyager 1 launched on its journey into the outer solar system.

09-06.text: Cal Ripken Jr. played his 2,131st consecutive game, breaking Lou Gehrig's record.

09-07.text: Philo Farnsworth demonstrated an electronic television system.

09-08.text: Star Trek debuted on American television with The Man Trap.

09-09.text: Elvis Presley made his first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show.

09-10.text: Abebe Bikila won the Olympic marathon in Rome while running barefoot.

09-11.text: The September 11 terrorist attacks struck the United States.

09-12.text: President John F. Kennedy gave his Moon-mission speech at Rice University.

09-13.text: IBM introduced the 305 RAMAC computer with disk storage.

09-14.text: Theodore Roosevelt became U.S. president following William McKinley's death.

09-15.text: The Soviet Union launched Zond 5 on a flight around the Moon and back to Earth.

09-16.text: Sydney's TCN-9 began regular television broadcasts.

09-17.text: The American Professional Football Association was organized in Canton, Ohio; it later became the NFL.

09-18.text: Guiding Light aired its final television episode after decades on radio and TV.

09-19.text: Scott Fahlman proposed smiling and frowning emoticons on a Carnegie Mellon message board.

09-20.text: Billie Jean King beat Bobby Riggs in tennis's Battle of the Sexes.

09-21.text: J.R.R. Tolkien's The Hobbit was published.

09-22.text: Brighton's Duke of York's Picture House opened.

09-24.text: Earl and Weldon Bascom staged an outdoor rodeo under electric lights.

09-25.text: The Little Rock Nine entered Central High School under U.S. Army protection.

09-26.text: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov judged a missile-warning alert to be a false alarm.

09-27.text: The European SMART-1 mission launched toward the Moon.

09-28.text: Wyoming Seminary and Mansfield played an early American football game under electric lights.

09-29.text: CERN, the European particle-physics research organization, was established.

10-01.text: Boston and Pittsburgh began the first modern World Series.

10-02.text: Thurgood Marshall was sworn in as the first Black justice of the U.S. Supreme Court.

10-03.text: Reds pitcher Adolfo Luque became the first Latin American player to appear in a World Series.

10-04.text: Sputnik 1 became Earth's first artificial satellite.

10-05.text: The Beatles released their first British single, Love Me Do.

10-06.text: The Jazz Singer opened, helping usher in the era of talking pictures.

10-07.text: Luna 3 photographed the far side of the Moon.

10-08.text: Don Larsen pitched a perfect game for the Yankees in the World Series.

10-09.text: Hoover Dam began sending electricity to Los Angeles.

10-10.text: The Tokyo Olympics opened with a ceremony relayed by satellite.

10-11.text: Apollo 7 launched, beginning the first crewed Apollo mission.

10-12.text: A Bavarian royal wedding began celebrations that became Munich's Oktoberfest tradition.

10-13.text: Boston beat Pittsburgh to win the first modern World Series.

10-14.text: Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier in the Bell X-1.

10-15.text: Tata Airlines, later known as Air India, made its first flight.

10-16.text: Walt and Roy Disney founded their cartoon studio.

10-17.text: Albert Einstein arrived in the United States after leaving Nazi Germany.

10-18.text: The British Broadcasting Company was founded.

10-19.text: Britain imposed restrictions on broadcasting the voices of members of several Northern Ireland organizations.

10-20.text: Queen Elizabeth II officially opened the Sydney Opera House.

10-21.text: Rams player Fred Dryer scored two safeties in one NFL game.

10-22.text: Andre-Jacques Garnerin made a pioneering parachute descent over Paris.

10-23.text: Apple introduced the iPod music player.

10-24.text: The Toronto Blue Jays became the first team outside the U.S. to win the World Series.

10-25.text: Tchaikovsky's First Piano Concerto premiered in Boston.

10-27.text: NASA launched its first Saturn I rocket on the SA-1 test flight.

10-28.text: President Grover Cleveland dedicated the Statue of Liberty.

10-29.text: ARPANET transmitted its first computer-to-computer message.

10-30.text: Orson Welles broadcast his radio adaptation of The War of the Worlds.

10-31.text: The transcontinental Lincoln Highway was dedicated.

11-01.text: Honda began producing cars at its Marysville, Ohio, factory.

11-02.text: Pittsburgh's KDKA broadcast the U.S. presidential election returns.

11-03.text: Sputnik 2 carried the dog Laika into Earth orbit.

11-04.text: Wyoming voters elected Nellie Tayloe Ross as governor.

11-05.text: Authorities arrested Guy Fawkes as the Gunpowder Plot was uncovered in London.

11-06.text: Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4 in an early intercollegiate football game.

11-07.text: An airplane carried freight from Dayton to Columbus, Ohio, in a landmark commercial shipment.

11-09.text: East Germany opened Berlin Wall checkpoints, allowing crowds to cross.

11-10.text: Sesame Street made its television debut.

11-11.text: The World War I armistice with Germany took effect.

11-12.text: Pudge Heffelfinger played a documented paid football game for Allegheny Athletic Association.

11-13.text: Disney's Fantasia premiered in New York City.

11-16.text: Oklahoma joined the United States as its 46th state.

11-17.text: NBC cut away from the Jets-Raiders game to show Heidi, causing eastern viewers to miss Oakland's comeback.

11-18.text: Disney's Steamboat Willie premiered, bringing Mickey Mouse to the screen with synchronized sound.

11-19.text: Abraham Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address.

11-21.text: WABC dismissed pioneering rock-and-roll DJ Alan Freed amid the payola scandal.

11-22.text: President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas.

11-23.text: Doctor Who made its BBC television debut.

11-24.text: Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species.

11-25.text: Albert Einstein presented the field equations of general relativity.

11-26.text: Casablanca premiered in New York City.

11-27.text: Penny Ann Early briefly played for the Kentucky Colonels in an ABA basketball game.

11-28.text: The radio show that became the Grand Ole Opry began as the WSM Barn Dance.

11-29.text: The Beatles released I Want to Hold Your Hand in Britain.

11-30.text: Space shuttle Endeavour launched on mission STS-97.

12-01.text: Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama.

12-02.text: Enrico Fermi's team achieved a self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction in Chicago.

12-03.text: An engineer sent the first SMS text message over Vodafone's network.

12-04.text: Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, Jerry Lee Lewis and Carl Perkins gathered at Sun Studio.

12-05.text: The 21st Amendment was ratified, ending U.S. Prohibition.

12-06.text: Construction of the Washington Monument was completed.

12-07.text: The Army-Navy football broadcast used instant replay.

12-08.text: Metallica performed in Antarctica, completing concerts on all seven continents in one year.

12-09.text: Coronation Street aired its first episode on British television.

12-10.text: The first Nobel Prize awards were presented.

12-12.text: Marconi reported receiving a radio signal from across the Atlantic in Newfoundland.

12-13.text: Abel Tasman's expedition sighted New Zealand.

12-14.text: Roald Amundsen's expedition reached the South Pole.

12-15.text: Gone with the Wind premiered in Atlanta.

12-16.text: Boston Tea Party protesters dumped shipments of tea into the harbor.

12-17.text: The Wright brothers made their historic powered flights at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

12-18.text: The Chicago Bears beat the Portsmouth Spartans in the NFL championship playoff.

12-19.text: The BBC Empire Service, later the World Service, began broadcasting.

12-20.text: The first production version of Boeing's 707 took flight.

12-21.text: Apollo 8 launched with astronauts bound for lunar orbit.

12-22.text: Beethoven's Fifth and Sixth Symphonies premiered at a concert in Vienna.

12-24.text: Apollo 8 entered lunar orbit, and its crew photographed Earthrise.

12-25.text: Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as president of the Soviet Union.

12-26.text: The Beatles' I Want to Hold Your Hand and I Saw Her Standing There were released in the U.S.

12-27.text: Charles Darwin set sail aboard HMS Beagle.

12-28.text: Maurice Richard became the first NHL player to score eight points in one game.

12-31.text: Thomas Edison gave a public demonstration of incandescent lighting at Menlo Park, New Jersey.
